message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"85139f8f50e790120bb29670fb3402c4570e8efa19678af75bfd876ae20ffba5","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mo-class-f:lineage:77","source_registry_sha256":"f128002157e581eb7004b9370c8cfbafd7b29a1596262980704fbda0a45932f5","units":[{"unit_id":"sec03-u01","module_id":"sec03-m01","objective_ids":["sec03-u01"],"title":{"text":"Exam parts and who tests","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Knowing the four parts of the examination tells you what to prepare for before your visit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]},{"text":"Not everyone takes every part, so it pays to know which route applies to you.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R05","sec03-F03"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Rosa moves to Missouri holding a valid license of the same type from her old state.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R05"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Her license is the same type and still valid, so she qualifies for the shortened route.","fact_ids":["sec03-R05"]},"result":{"text":"She takes only the vision and road sign tests.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a current license always excuses you from the examination.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]},"correction":{"text":"The Director of Revenue can require the examination even when your license is current.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Four parts; the transfer route needs same type and recent enough.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-R05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A new resident holds a valid license of the same type from another state. Which tests does she take?","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R05"]},"answer":{"text":"Only the vision and road sign tests.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R05"]},"rationale":{"text":"A same-type license that is valid or expired less than one hundred eighty-four days qualifies for the shortened route.","fact_ids":["sec03-R05","sec03-F02"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"The Missouri driver examination","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F03","sec03-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Four parts.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F03","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Who must take them.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F03","sec03-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the chapter on the driver examination. Before you can drive on your own, you need to know what the examination contains and whether all of it applies to you. This lesson covers the four parts of the examination, the situations that require it, the revocations that send a driver back through it, and the shortened route for some drivers who hold a license from another state. You will also learn who gives the examination, what identification you need, and where to find testing locations. Knowing all of this ahead of time makes your visit to the testing center far less stressful.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F03","sec03-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Four parts of the exam","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Written test on laws and safe driving.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]},{"text":"Vision test and road sign test.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]},{"text":"Driving skills test.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"The Missouri driver examination has four parts. There is a written test on traffic laws and safe-driving rules, a vision test, a road sign test, and a driving skills test. Each part checks something different: what you know, how well you see, whether you recognize signs, and how you actually handle a car. Later lessons in this chapter go through each part in detail. For now, remember the list of four, because questions about which tests a driver must take build on it. If you can name the four parts, you can sort out every route through the examination that follows.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"When the exam is required","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"New Missouri license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},{"text":"Expired more than six months.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},{"text":"Director asks, or certain revocations.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"The examination is required in several situations. You take it for a new Missouri license. You take it if your Missouri license has been expired more than six months, which the guide counts as one hundred eighty-four days. The Director of Revenue can also require it at any time, even if your license is current. And a license revoked for too many points or for an Administrative Alcohol action sends the driver back through the examination as well. So the examination is not only for beginners; long expirations, revocations and a request from the Director can all bring it back into your life.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The out-of-state shortcut","fact_ids":["sec03-R05","sec03-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Same type of license.","fact_ids":["sec03-R05","sec03-F02"]},{"text":"Valid or recently expired.","fact_ids":["sec03-R05","sec03-F02"]},{"text":"Then only vision and signs.","fact_ids":["sec03-R05","sec03-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. Some drivers think any out-of-state license lets them skip most of the examination. The shortened route has two conditions. The license must be for the same type of license you are applying for in Missouri, and it must be valid or expired less than one hundred eighty-four days. If both are true, you take only the vision and road sign tests. If either one fails, for example a different license type or a license expired too long ago, the shortcut does not apply. On a test, check both conditions before choosing the shorter route.","fact_ids":["sec03-R05","sec03-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the transfer route","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"New resident, same-type license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R05"]},{"text":"License still valid.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R05"]},{"text":"Which tests?","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a new resident arrives in Missouri with a valid license of the same type from her old state. Which parts of the examination does she take? Work it out before reading on. The answer is only the vision and road sign tests. Her license meets both conditions of the shortened route: it is the same type of license, and it is valid rather than expired more than one hundred eighty-four days. If her license had been a different type, or had been expired for longer than that, she would take the full examination like any new applicant.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Who gives the exam","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-R16"]},"lines":[{"text":"The Highway Patrol gives it.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-R16"]},{"text":"Bring proof of name and age.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-R16"]},{"text":"Locations at the back and online.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-R16"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, the Missouri State Highway Patrol gives the driver examination, and either the Patrol or the Department can point you to the nearest testing center. The phone numbers for both are printed at the back of the guide, and testing locations are also listed on the Highway Patrol website. Before the examination you must prove your legal name and age, and you show that identification again whenever you apply for a license or permit and each time you take the written or driving test. Next, you will look closely at the written test and the road sign test.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-R16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u02","module_id":"sec03-m02","objective_ids":["sec03-u02"],"title":{"text":"Written and road sign tests","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The written test checks your knowledge of the laws and driving methods in the guide.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07"]},{"text":"The rules for the written test differ by license class, so it helps to know which applies to you.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Tom, applying for a Class F license, plans to bring the guide into the written test.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08"]},"reasoning":{"text":"The written test is not open book, so the guide cannot be used.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-R04"]},"result":{"text":"Tom studies beforehand and leaves the guide at home.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking the Class E test is open book because it is longer.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04"]},"correction":{"text":"Both the Class F and Class E written tests are closed book; only Class E adds the commercial chapter.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04","sec03-F09"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Both closed book; E adds commercial.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"An applicant for a Class E for-hire license asks if his written test is open book. What is the answer?","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]},"answer":{"text":"No. The Class E test is also closed book, and it adds the commercial vehicle chapter.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]},"rationale":{"text":"Both written tests are closed book; the difference is that only the Class E test includes the commercial material.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04","sec03-F09"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Knowledge tests","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},"lines":[{"text":"The written test.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},{"text":"The road sign test.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers the two knowledge tests in the examination: the written test and the road sign test. You will learn how the Class F written test is set up, what it covers and what it leaves out, and whether you may use the guide during it. You will also see how the test changes for a Class E for-hire applicant, what the road sign test checks, and the serious penalty for any kind of fraud during an examination. These are some of the simplest facts in the guide, but they are easy to mix up, so the lesson points out the contrasts as it goes along.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The Class F written test","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Twenty-five multiple-choice questions.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]},{"text":"Laws and driving methods in the guide.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]},{"text":"Not open book.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"The Class F written test has twenty-five multiple-choice questions on the laws and driving methods this guide covers. It is not open book, so you cannot look things up during the test, and a Class F applicant is not tested on the commercial vehicle material in the commercial vehicle chapter. That means your study time should go to the rest of the guide: the license rules, the rules of the road, signs, safe driving, alcohol and the other chapters. Studying the whole guide, rather than guessing what might be asked, is the most reliable way to prepare for a closed-book test.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The Class E for-hire test","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"A special written test.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]},{"text":"Adds the commercial chapter.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]},{"text":"Also not open book.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"A Class E for-hire applicant takes a special written test. It adds the commercial vehicle material from the commercial vehicle chapter on top of the regular content, and like the Class F test, it is not open book. So a Class E applicant has more to study, but the rule about bringing materials is the same. The difference between the two tests is only about content, not about whether you may use the guide. If you are applying for a Class F license, the commercial chapter is not on your test, and if you are applying for Class E for hire, it is.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Closed book for both","fact_ids":["sec03-R04","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Class F: closed book.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},{"text":"Class E: closed book too.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},{"text":"Only Class E adds commercial.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Because the Class E test covers more, some learners assume it must be different in other ways, perhaps open book. It is not. Both the Class F and the Class E written tests are closed book. The single difference is that only the Class E test includes the commercial vehicle chapter. If a question asks which test is open book, the answer is neither. If it asks which test includes commercial vehicle material, the answer is the Class E for-hire test. Keep the shared rule and the one difference side by side in your mind.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Road signs and honesty","fact_ids":["sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},"lines":[{"text":"Recognize signs and their meaning.","fact_ids":["sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},{"text":"Fraud is a Class A misdemeanor.","fact_ids":["sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},{"text":"It can cost up to one year.","fact_ids":["sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]}],"narration":{"text":"The road sign test checks whether you can recognize traffic signs and understand what they mean, so study the shapes, colors and messages in the signs chapter. The guide also warns about fraud in any license, permit or nondriver ID examination. False statements, cheating, or using a recording, a camera or a two-way communication device all count. Fraud is a Class A misdemeanor, and it can cost your driving privilege for up to one year. The honest path is also the easier one: study the guide, take the tests on your own, and earn the license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the Class E rule","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Class E for-hire applicant.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]},{"text":"Open book or not?","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: an applicant for a Class E for-hire license asks whether he may bring the guide into his written test, since his test covers more material. What do you tell him? Work it out before reading on. The answer is no. The Class E for-hire written test is also closed book. What makes it different is that it adds the commercial vehicle chapter to the regular content. So he should study the commercial chapter along with the rest of the guide, and leave the book at home on test day, just as a Class F applicant would.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Knowledge tests recap","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-R04","sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},"lines":[{"text":"Twenty-five questions, closed book.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-R04","sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},{"text":"Class E adds commercial.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-R04","sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},{"text":"Sign test and fraud rule.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-R04","sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us recap. The Class F written test has twenty-five multiple-choice questions on the laws and driving methods in the guide. It is closed book and leaves out the commercial vehicle chapter. The Class E for-hire test is also closed book but adds that commercial material. The road sign test checks that you recognize signs and know what they mean. Any fraud during an examination is a Class A misdemeanor that can cost your driving privilege for up to one year. In the next lesson, you will learn how the vision test works and what levels you need.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-R04","sec03-F16","sec03-F38"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u03","module_id":"sec03-m03","objective_ids":["sec03-u03"],"title":{"text":"The vision test","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-R01"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Safe driving depends on seeing clearly ahead and to the sides, so both are tested.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"Knowing the standards and the cutoffs helps you understand what a vision result means.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F15","sec03-R03"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ben's acuity is twenty or forty in both eyes, and his side vision is sixty degrees in each eye.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Twenty or forty meets the acuity standard, and fifty-five degrees or more in each eye meets the side vision standard.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12"]},"result":{"text":"Ben passes both vision screens.","fact_ids":["sec03-R01"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: treating twenty or one hundred sixty as the passing acuity.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03"]},"correction":{"text":"Twenty or forty is the standard; twenty or one hundred sixty is the cutoff below which no license is possible when both natural and corrected vision are worse.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F11","sec03-F15"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Twenty forty to pass; twenty one-sixty and seventy combined are the floors.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F15"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Is twenty or one hundred sixty the acuity you need to pass the standard vision test?","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F11"]},"answer":{"text":"No. The standard is twenty or forty or better; twenty or one hundred sixty is the cutoff for any license.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F11"]},"rationale":{"text":"The cutoff applies only when both natural and corrected acuity are worse than it, and it marks where no license is possible.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F15"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Seeing well enough to drive","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two vision screens.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-F15"]},{"text":"Standards and cutoffs.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers the vision test. Every applicant for a new or renewal license or permit takes it, and it has two separate parts: a test of how sharply you see, called acuity, and a test of your side vision, called peripheral vision. You will learn the standard levels for each, what happens if you do not meet them, and the lower cutoffs below which a Missouri license is not possible at all. The numbers in this lesson are easy to confuse, so we will keep the standard levels and the cutoffs clearly apart as we work through them together.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Two separate screens","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Acuity measures sharpness.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"Peripheral measures side vision.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"Every new or renewal applicant.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every new or renewal license or permit applicant takes both an acuity test and a peripheral, or side, vision test. Acuity is how sharply you see details, such as letters on a chart. Side vision is how much you notice off to the left and right while looking straight ahead. Each is measured separately. That matters because passing one screen does not cover the other. A driver with sharp acuity can still fall short on side vision, and the other way around. So when you think about the vision test, think of it as two tests that both need to be passed.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The standard levels","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Acuity: twenty forty or better.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13"]},{"text":"Side: fifty-five each eye.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13"]},{"text":"Or eighty-five in one eye.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here are the standard minimums. For acuity, the standard is twenty or forty or better, using either eye or both eyes. For side vision, the standard is fifty-five degrees or more in each eye, or eighty-five degrees or more in one eye. Notice that side vision has two routes to pass: both eyes at fifty-five or more, or one eye at eighty-five or more. If you meet these levels you pass the screen. If you do not, the result can be a denied license or restrictions placed on the license, so the vision test matters as much as the others.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"If you fail the screen","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Vision exam form for a specialist.","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F13"]},{"text":"New glasses may mean waiting.","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F13"]},{"text":"Then the other tests.","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"If you fail the standard vision test, the examiner hands you a vision exam form to take to an eye specialist or a physician. The specialist examines your eyes and completes the form. If you end up with a new prescription, you may have to wait for the new glasses or contacts before you take the written or driving test. So a failed screen is not always the end of the road. Missing the standards can lead to a denied license or to restrictions placed on the license, such as a requirement to wear corrective lenses, depending on what the results show.","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Standard versus cutoff","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F15","sec03-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Twenty forty is the standard.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F15","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"Twenty one-sixty is a cutoff.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F15","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"Seventy degrees combined is the floor.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F15","sec03-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. The guide gives two sets of numbers, and learners often swap them. The standard passing acuity is twenty or forty. The figure twenty or one hundred sixty is not a passing level; it is the cutoff. If both your natural and your corrected acuity are worse than twenty or one hundred sixty, you cannot take the driving test or hold a Missouri license. Side vision has a similar floor: if your combined side vision is worse than seventy degrees, no license is possible. Standards decide pass or fail on the screen, while cutoffs decide whether any license is possible.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F15","sec03-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the acuity numbers","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F11","sec03-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Twenty or one hundred sixty.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F11","sec03-F15"]},{"text":"Passing level or cutoff?","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F11","sec03-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a friend says she only needs twenty or one hundred sixty acuity to pass the standard vision test. Is she right? Work it out before reading on. She is not. The standard passing acuity is twenty or forty or better, using either eye or both eyes. Twenty or one hundred sixty is the cutoff that matters only when both natural and corrected acuity are worse than it, and at that point no Missouri license is possible. So twenty or forty is the level to aim for, and twenty or one hundred sixty is the floor below which a license is ruled out.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F11","sec03-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Vision test recap","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-F12","sec03-F14","sec03-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two screens, both needed.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-F12","sec03-F14","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"Know standards from cutoffs.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-F12","sec03-F14","sec03-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us sum up the vision test. Every new or renewal applicant takes two screens, acuity and side vision, and passing one does not cover the other. The standards are twenty or forty or better for acuity, and fifty-five degrees in each eye or eighty-five in one eye for side vision. A failed screen leads to a vision exam form for a specialist, and missing the standards can mean denial or restrictions. Below twenty or one hundred sixty acuity with and without correction, or seventy degrees combined side vision, no license is possible.
